D: A mafia patriarch hands the family business to his reluctant youngest son.
P: Pour the Chianti when the wedding band starts up in the opening scene.
S: salami, provolone, olives and roast peppers laid out like the garden party

Roast two red capsicums black over a flame, sweat in a covered bowl, peel and dress with garlic, red wine vinegar and oil. Platter with folded finocchiona and sopressa, wedges of aged provolone, Sicilian green olives and grissini wrapped in prosciutto.
for all those oranges on screen, every one a warning

Segment 4 blood or navel oranges over a bowl to catch the juice. Shave 1 fennel bulb and half a red onion paper thin, toss with the segments, black olives, fennel fronds, the juice, good olive oil, flaky salt and chilli flakes.
the kind of starter Clemenza would order without looking at a menu

Cut cleaned squid tubes into rings, soak 30 minutes in buttermilk. Dredge in half fine semolina, half flour with salt and pepper, fry at 190C for 90 seconds in small batches. Lemon wedges and a quick marinara for dipping.
M: fry the garlic, tomatoes and paste, brown the sausage and meatballs, a splash of wine, a little sugar

Fennel sausage and pork and beef meatballs browned hard, then slow-simmered in San Marzano gravy with garlic and red wine, over rigatoni with pecorino. Mix 400g pork and beef mince with 1 egg, 40g breadcrumbs, 30g grated pecorino and a pinch of salt; form 12 meatballs. Brown in olive oil with 3 fennel sausages cut into chunks; set aside. Soften 1 diced onion, add 3 sliced garlic cloves and 2 tbsp tomato paste. Stir in 800g tinned tomatoes and 200ml water. Return meat, cover partly and simmer gently 60 to 90 minutes, stirring and adding water if needed. Check meatballs are cooked through. Boil 400g rigatoni, toss with sauce and serve with the meat and another 30g pecorino.
lemon and capers, the best veal in the city, so Sollozzo says

Pound veal escalopes to 4mm, season, dust in flour. Sear 60 seconds a side in butter and oil, rest on a plate. Deglaze with white wine, add lemon juice, capers and stock, reduce, swirl in cold butter, return the veal and parsley.
W: take the cannoli, it's the one thing everyone remembers

Drain 500g fresh ricotta overnight in muslin. Beat with 80g icing sugar, orange zest and vanilla, fold in mini choc chips. Pipe into bought cannoli shells just before serving so they stay crisp, dip the ends in crushed pistachio, dust with icing sugar.
K: the straw bottle on the table, and the oranges that turn up before every hit

Chianti steeped with sliced oranges, lemon, a cinnamon stick and a splash of brandy, topped with soda over ice. Slice 2 oranges and 1 lemon into a large jug. Add 1 cinnamon stick, 60ml brandy and 40g caster sugar and muddle gently for 30 seconds. Pour in 750ml Chianti, stir until the sugar dissolves and refrigerate for 2 hours. Just before serving, add 300ml chilled soda water and stir once. Pour over ice into tumblers with a slice of orange in each.

dishes.make_ahead: Make the risotto up to 1 day ahead; shape and crumb up to 4 hours ahead, keep chilled

steps.text: Cut the mozzarella into 8 cubes. Divide the cold risotto into 8 portions and wrap each around a cube, rolling into balls.
Roll the balls in flour, dip in the beaten egg and coat in breadcrumbs.
Chill the crumbed balls for 20 minutes so they hold their shape.
Heat the oil to 170C and fry in batches until golden and hot through, about 4 to 5 minutes. Drain and finish with the sea salt.

steps.text: Fry the mushrooms in 1 tbsp of the olive oil until dry and browned, then cool.
Mix the mushrooms with the ricotta, egg, breadcrumbs, a share of the cheese and the salt. Form 12 meatballs and chill.
Brown the meatballs gently in the rest of the oil with the sausages cut into chunks, then set aside.
Soften the onion in the same pot, add the garlic and tomato paste, then stir in the tomatoes and water. Cover partly and simmer gently for 45 minutes, stirring and adding water if needed.
Return the meatballs and sausages and simmer for 15 minutes without stirring hard.
Boil the rigatoni, toss with the sauce and serve with the meatballs and the rest of the cheese.

s.note: Salami, aged provolone, olives and roast peppers.
s.how: Arrange 100g sliced salami, 100g aged provolone, 100g olives and 150g drained roast capsicum on a platter. Drizzle the capsicum with olive oil and add a little cracked pepper. Serve at room temperature while the main simmers.

s.note: Crumbed risotto balls with a molten mozzarella centre, fried golden and served hot with a pinch of sea salt.
s.how: Use 400g cold, thick cooked risotto. Divide into 8 portions and wrap each around a cube cut from 80g mozzarella. Roll into balls, dust with 40g flour, dip in 1 beaten egg and coat in 80g breadcrumbs. Chill 20 minutes. Fry in 170°C neutral oil in batches until golden and hot throughout, about 4 to 5 minutes; drain. Make the risotto the day before, cool promptly and refrigerate, or use 8 ready-made mozzarella arancini following the packet instructions.

m.note: Fennel sausage and pork and beef meatballs browned hard, then slow-simmered in San Marzano gravy with garlic and red wine, over rigatoni with pecorino.

Soften 1 diced onion, add 3 sliced garlic cloves and 2 tbsp tomato paste. Stir in 800g tinned tomatoes and 200ml water. Return meat, cover partly and simmer gently 60 to 90 minutes, stirring and adding water if needed. Check meatballs are cooked through. w.note: Crisp shells, orange-scented ricotta, dark chocolate and crushed pistachio.
w.how: Drain 250g ricotta in a lined sieve in the fridge for at least 2 hours. Beat with 40g icing sugar and zest of 1 orange; fold in 30g finely chopped dark chocolate. Pipe into 8 small bought cannoli shells just before serving. Dip ends into 30g crushed pistachios and dust lightly with icing sugar.

d.note: Blood orange syrup, sparkling water and a fresh orange twist.
d.how: Fill 4 glasses with ice. Add 25ml blood orange syrup to each and top each with 200ml sparkling water. Stir gently and finish with a thin twist from 1 orange. Adjust syrup to taste.
